title: Seed Database
summary: Writes a seed script with realistic, properly related sample data that is safe to run twice and refuses to run in production.
description: Empty tables make every screen look broken, and random strings make demos look fake. This command reads your schema and writes a seed script with believable names, valid foreign keys and a mix of normal and edge-case rows.
The script is idempotent, so running it again does not duplicate anything, and it stops itself when pointed at anything that looks like production.
useWhen: A new hire needs a database that works on day one
You want realistic demo data for a screenshot or sales call
Tests need the same starting rows every time
A new feature needs related data across many tables
body:
Write a seed script for: $ARGUMENTS (tables, feature, or "all").

1. Read the schema, models and migrations. Map the tables, their foreign keys, unique keys, enums and required fields. Note the project's seed convention (prisma/seed.ts, db/seeds.rb, fixtures, a management command) and follow it.
2. Plan the insert order from parents to children. Use realistic values: plausible names, emails at example.com, dates over the last year, prices with sensible ranges. Add edge cases deliberately: a long name, a null optional field, an inactive user, a zero-total order.
3. Make it idempotent: upsert on a natural key or truncate only seed-owned rows, using a fixed random seed so data is the same every run.
4. Add a guard: abort if the database URL contains prod or a non-local host unless `ALLOW_SEED=1`.
5. Never use real customer data and never write secrets or real passwords. Hash a known dev password.

Print row counts per table and the command to run it. Do not run it until the user confirms which database it points to.

example.result:
Wrote prisma/seed.ts: 25 customers, 60 products in 6 categories, 140 orders with 1 to 5 items. Includes one refunded order and one customer with no orders.
Upserts by email and sku, seed fixed at 42, aborts on non-local URLs.
Run npx prisma db seed against localhost?

faq.question: Can I run it twice?
faq.answer: Yes. Rows are upserted on stable keys, so a second run leaves the same data.

faq.question: Could it touch my production database?
faq.answer: The script refuses to run when the connection string looks remote or production, unless you set an explicit override.

access: Creates a seed script and runs it only after you confirm the target database
